card.name: Second drug in interaction statements
card.fires_on: The end of a drug name, or the word 'and' after one, in drug-interaction text where one drug's effect on another has just been described. The spot is where a reverse effect (the other drug acting on the first) might come next.

modes.label: Inside or end of affected drug name
modes.description: Part or end of the name of the drug whose levels or effects are changed by another drug.
modes.example: increased plasma concentrations of<< flu>>conazole by 40%.

modes.label: Linking 'and' or noun after drug
modes.description: The word 'and' or a product noun right after a drug name, before a second clause about the drug pair.
modes.example: may reduce the effect of miglitol tablets<< and>> should not be taken concomitantly

card.writes: It pushes toward words that introduce the reverse relation, such as 'vice (versa)', 'conversely', 'reciprocal' and 'likewise'.
card.plain: It fires in interaction passages after a drug name, where the text could go on to say the reverse also holds.
